article_blocks.text: Strain Type: Indica-leaning hybrid
Genetics: Ice Cream Cake × Grape Pie × Wedding Crasher
Breeder: Bloom Seed Co.
THC Content: 25-28%
CBD Content: Typically trace to less than 1%
Terpene Profile: Myrcene , limonene , beta-caryophyllene
Primary Flavors: Candy grape, vanilla cream, sweet dough
Flowering Time (Indoor): 9–10 weeks
Outdoor Harvest Time: early to mid-October
Indoor Yield: Moderate to high
Outdoor Yield: Moderate to high
Grow Difficulty: Moderate

Some marijuana strains announce themselves with skunk, fuel, or sharp citrus. Dulce De Uva takes another route, opening with the impression of a confectionery counter stocked with grape candy, vanilla frosting, and freshly mixed cake batter before a layer of gas reminds you that this is still potent cannabis. The name translates roughly to “grape sweet,” and few modern cultivars fit their name so neatly.

Developed by Bloom Seed Co., this resin-rich hybrid combines dessert-oriented genetics with the structure and potency expected from contemporary boutique weed. Its appeal extends beyond flower alone: abundant resin production and an unusually distinctive grape-and-dough terpene profile have also made the cultivar valuable for solventless concentrates and breeding projects. Rather than delivering a purely sleepy indica experience, the high generally develops in stages, beginning with an upbeat mental shift before gradually moving toward heavier physical relaxation.
Genetics and Lineage

Bloom Seed Co. lists the authentic lineage as Ice Cream Cake × (Grape Pie × Wedding Crasher). This breeder-confirmed parentage is important because alternate genetic descriptions have circulated under the same strain name. Bloom’s own material identifies Ice Cream Cake as one side of the cross and the combination of Grape Pie and Wedding Crasher as the other.

Each branch contributes something recognizable to the finished cultivar. Ice Cream Cake supplies creamy dessert character, dense flower formation, substantial THC potential, and an inclination toward body relaxation. Grape Pie reinforces dark fruit, berry sweetness, and purple-flower tendencies, while Wedding Crasher brings vanilla, pastry-like sweetness, and additional vigor. Together, those traits produce cannabis that can smell dramatically sweeter than its potency might suggest. The genetic combination has proved useful enough that Bloom has subsequently incorporated Dulce De Uva into crosses such as Black Maple and Grape Rips, giving the cultivar an increasingly visible place in modern breeding work.
Effects and Experience

The initial portion of the experience tends to be considerably brighter than the dessert-heavy genetics might imply. A moderate amount can bring a noticeable lift in mood, a looser conversational quality, and a pleasantly altered headspace without immediately shutting down concentration. Humor may seem more engaging, music can become more immersive, and ordinary activities may acquire the relaxed novelty associated with euphoric cannabis. With higher-THC examples, however, that first wave can arrive quickly, making measured consumption sensible for people with limited marijuana tolerance.

Physical calm becomes increasingly prominent as the session develops. Muscle tension may seem to recede, the body feels heavier against a chair or couch, and the energetic side of the high gives way to an easier pace. This progression makes the cultivar more naturally suited to late afternoon or evening than a demanding workday. Larger doses may deepen the sedation considerably, while smaller quantities can preserve more of the sociable, happy character at the beginning. Potency should never be assumed from the strain name alone: tested flower has reached the mid-to-upper 20% THC range, demonstrating why product-specific laboratory results matter when available.
Medical Benefits

Medical marijuana consumers may find the combination of mental decompression and physical relaxation useful when trying to manage certain symptoms, particularly stress, persistent tension, difficulty settling down, appetite changes, or discomfort that interferes with relaxation. Its gradually increasing body effect may be especially appealing during the evening, when stimulation is no longer desirable and the objective is simply to become comfortable. Some consumers also favor euphoric strains during periods of low mood because the early phase can feel emotionally lighter before the heavier body component takes hold.

These uses should be viewed as potential symptom-management applications rather than established treatments for specific diseases. Cannabis responses vary according to THC dose, tolerance, individual physiology, terpene composition, medications, and method of consumption. Someone prone to THC-related anxiety may find a strong batch uncomfortable despite the strain’s generally relaxing reputation. Dry mouth and dry eyes are common possibilities, while excessive consumption may result in dizziness, temporary anxiety, impaired coordination, or pronounced drowsiness.
Flavor Profile and Aroma

Grape is the defining theme, but describing the profile as simply fruity misses much of its character. Breaking apart well-cured flower can release a concentrated sweet-grape aroma resembling purple candy, grape syrup, or berry preserves. Beneath that sweetness sits creamy dough, vanilla cake, and a faintly sour gasoline edge. Bloom Seed Co. summarizes the expression as sweet candy grape over doughy gas, an unusually concise description that captures the contrast between its confectionery opening and danker finish.

The terpene composition helps explain why different batches can lean in slightly different directions. Laboratory-tested flower has shown meaningful levels of myrcene and limonene alongside beta-caryophyllene, linalool, and humulene. One flower analysis recorded myrcene and limonene as the two largest components, followed by beta-caryophyllene and linalool, while another batch placed limonene ahead of myrcene. That variation can shift the aroma from jammy and creamy toward brighter citrus-grape or peppery gas. On the palate, expect the grape sweetness to arrive first, followed by vanilla pastry, earthy spice, and a lingering dough-and-fuel aftertaste.
Growing Information

Dulce De Uva deserves more attention in vegetative growth than its dessert-strain reputation might suggest. Bloom specifically advises controlling stretch through training and recommends flowering the plant with numerous tops rather than allowing a few dominant branches to take over. Multiple trellis layers can help organize the canopy and support developing flowers. The breeder gives a flowering period of approximately 9–10 weeks, placing it within a manageable window for modern photoperiod cannabis cultivation.

Canopy planning becomes especially important as the plant transitions into bloom. Early topping, low-stress training, or similar methods can distribute growth across a wider footprint and improve light penetration. Adequate airflow around maturing buds is equally important wherever dense flowers develop, particularly during the later weeks when humidity can become problematic. Under strong lighting and a dialed-in environment, yield can be respectable, although Bloom emphasizes the cultivar’s high solventless return more explicitly than a standardized dried-flower yield. Resin production is one of the plant’s major strengths, making careful handling near harvest worthwhile for growers interested in preserving trichome quality. Outdoor cultivation is possible where autumn weather remains dry enough to finish a roughly 9–10 week flowering cycle.
FAQ
Is Dulce De Uva an indica or sativa?

It is generally regarded as an indica-leaning hybrid. The experience often begins with noticeable cerebral euphoria before gradually developing into stronger physical relaxation, so it does not behave like an immediately sedating pure indica.
What are the genetics of Dulce De Uva?

Bloom Seed Co. identifies the lineage as Ice Cream Cake × (Grape Pie × Wedding Crasher). That breeder-confirmed pedigree distinguishes the original cultivar from other grape-themed marijuana genetics sometimes sold under similar names.
What does Dulce De Uva taste like?

Candy grape is the dominant flavor, accompanied by vanilla, creamy cake batter, berry sweetness, dough, and gas. Some batches show additional citrus, pepper, floral, or earthy accents depending on their terpene balance.
How strong is Dulce De Uva?

It can be quite potent. Commercial flower has tested in the mid-to-upper 20% THC range, although cannabinoid levels are not genetically fixed and can change substantially between growers and harvests. Checking the laboratory label on the specific product is more reliable than assuming one universal THC percentage.
How long does Dulce De Uva take to flower?

Bloom Seed Co. gives the original cultivar a 9–10 week indoor flowering period. The breeder also recommends controlling its stretch during vegetative growth and using multiple layers of trellis support to create a productive canopy.
Final Thoughts on Dulce De Uva

Dulce De Uva occupies an appealing intersection of modern dessert cannabis and serious resin-focused breeding. Its Ice Cream Cake, Grape Pie, and Wedding Crasher ancestry produces a profile built around concentrated grape sweetness, creamy dough, vanilla, and enough gas to keep the flavor from becoming one-dimensional. The effects are similarly layered: an initially cheerful, sociable mental shift gradually gives way to deeper physical calm, making this weed particularly well suited to unwinding later in the day.

Growers have additional reasons to pay attention. A 9–10 week flowering cycle is manageable, resin production can be impressive, and strategic training can turn its stretch into a broad canopy of productive tops. Combined with its distinctive terpene character and strong potency potential, those qualities explain why the genetics have moved beyond a single cultivar and into numerous newer Bloom breeding projects. For anyone interested in contemporary grape-forward cannabis, Dulce De Uva represents far more than another sweet strain—it is one of the more distinctive examples of how dessert genetics, hash-oriented selection, and modern breeding can converge in the same plant.
